claim: Concretions and calcospherites grow by radial deposition about a centre (Harting's artificial concretions in egg albumen mimic natural ones), giving concentric/spherical forms by physical deposition alone.

dataset.name: Thompson (1917) On Growth and Form 1st ed., Ch. IX plates after Harting (1872): Figs. 195-197 (pp. 421-422) and 208-209 (p. 432), Internet Archive scan ongrowthform1917thom; analogues: Carmel Fm. ooids (Commons, PD) and Ag2CrO4 Liesegang rings in gelatine (Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0)
dataset.match: MATCH — the plates are Thompson's reproductions of the very Harting specimens named in the claim; Commons files are labelled analogues

caveats: 'Physical deposition alone' yields spherical forms in the interface-controlled (colloid-damped) regime; under diffusion-limited supply the same model gives spinous DLA forms, exactly the qualification Thompson himself makes on p. 424.

The ooid rounds off faster than uniform normal deposition predicts (minor-axis cortex thicker than major-axis cortex), so natural concretions need curvature- or agitation-dependent accretion on top of E3.
Fig. 195 nucleus centres and the Fig. 208 nucleus are manual landmarks (pinned in the script); all measurements about them are automated.
Harting (1872) is reached through Thompson's reproductions and the 1872 QJMS abstract, not the original plates.
